title: Find processes run by a specific user
summary: Use pgrep with the -u flag to find processes owned by a specific user. This is helpful for identifying which processes a particular user is running.

steps.explain: Use the -u flag followed by the username to filter processes by the user who started them. You can also specify a process name to narrow down the results.

placeholders.name: USERNAME
placeholders.description: The username whose processes you want to find

placeholders.name: PROCESS_NAME
placeholders.description: The name of the process to search for (optional, leave empty for all processes)
